newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish Hells Angel killed in Nordic biker war.
newsitem.headline: Danish Hells Angel killed in Nordic biker war.

text.p: Gunmen in the Danish town of Aalborg shot dead a member of the Hells Angels motorcycle gang overnight, bringing to eight the toll of death in a three-year Nordic biker war, police said on Saturday.

Police in the small town, in the north of the Jutland peninsula, said that 26-year-old Kim Svendsen was driving in the town's eastern suburbs on Friday night when another vehicle pulled alongside and an occupant fired at Svendsen, killing him and wounding a passenger, Lars Nielsen, 26.
Police raided the homes of known members of the rival Bandidos gang in and around Aalborg, where both gangs have branches.
"We have detained 14 people for questioning," a police officer said.

Police suspected that the killing may have been a response to the December shooting in Aalborg of a Bandidos member who was seriously wounded as he sat in a car in the town centre by shots fired from a passing vehicle.
A 23-year-old man with ties to the Hells Angels was later jailed for the attack.

The two gangs, both offshoots of U.S. bike clans, have been battling over turf in Denmark, Finland, Norway and Sweden since shortly after the Bandidos established themselves in the region in the summer of 1993.
The biker feud claimed its first life in February 1994, when a member of the Hells Angels-affiliated Rednecks died in a gunfight with Bandidos in the Swedish port of Helsingborg.
Two more Bandidos died over the following two years, in Sweden and in Finland, but on March 10 1996 the fighting took on a new intensity.

Gunmen outside Copenhagen International airport shot dead Danish Bandidos leader Uffe Larsen and wounded three of his companions as they waited to meet fellow-members returning from a visit to Helsinki.
A Copenhagen court, sitting in the tightest security ever seen in Denmark, jailed two Hells Angels for the killing last month.
A Danish Bandido was shot dead near the Norwegian city of Drammen in July.

Last October, as Danish legislators put the finishing touches to legislation to clamp down on the warring gangs, attackers fired an anti-tank missile into Hells Angels central Copenhagen clubhouse while it was packed with partygoers.
A gang member and a woman party guest unconnected with the gang died in the blast.
